fyPerformance: Gross advances reached ₹1.58 lakh Cr (+13.1% YoY); non-EEB advances grew about 20% and secured portfolio was 57.3% of advances, up from 54.9% a year earlier.

Deposits were ₹1.73 lakh Cr (+9.2% YoY; +4.7% QoQ). Retail deposits grew 11.9% YoY and retail term deposits 16.8%; CASA was ₹46,132 Cr and 26.7% of deposits. Net CD ratio was 89.5% versus about 92% in Q1.
NII was ₹2,960 Cr (+14.4% YoY); NIM was 6.1% versus 6.2% in Q1. Net total income was ₹3,655 Cr (+17%), operating profit ₹1,556 Cr (+18.8%) and PAT ₹622 Cr (5.5x YoY per management).
GNPA/NNPA were 3.1%/0.9%; credit cost was 1.8%. PCR was 71.2% excluding technical write-offs and 74.3% including security-receipt provisions. ROA/ROE were 1.2%/9.3%.
Bandhan Bank Ltd.whatChanged: Q2 loan growth was modest sequentially, with EEB contraction arrested and non-EEB/secured growth carrying the mix; deposits improved sequentially but savings-balance outflows and funding costs remain watchpoints. Management maintained roughly 14% FY27 loan growth and a Q4 exit ROA range of 1.2–1.4%.
risks: Savings balances saw outflows after rate-bucket recalibration; deposits grew more slowly than advances and the net CD ratio remains elevated at 89.5%.
EEB growth has stabilized but recovery is not yet a sustained growth trend; management described near-term housing growth disruption and continued elevated funding/technology costs.
ECL transition is estimated at about ₹2,200 Cr from the March 2026 estimate, to be absorbed through capital over five years; management said the estimate will be refreshed using the March 2027 book.
highlights: The secured/non-EEB portfolio supported diversification; EEB was ₹52,616 Cr, nearly flat sequentially and +1.7% YoY, while non-EEB was about two-thirds of advances.
Collections excluding NPAs were 99.4%; EEB collections were 99.3%. Gross slippages were ₹1,125 Cr, recoveries/upgrades ₹481 Cr, and GNPA was 3.1%.
Management retained its Q4 exit ROA goal of 1.2–1.4%, with funding and technology costs weighing on the recovery.

fyPerformance: Advances grew 21% YoY and deposits 19%; both had doubled over September 2022 in four years, as management noted. Revenue grew 21%, operating profit 26% and PAT 29% YoY.
Net profit was ₹236 Cr, the highest quarterly result to date; ROA was 1.03% for Q2 and 1.00% for H1; ROE was 14.6% for Q2 and 14.12% for H1.

Cost-to-average-assets was 2.47%, cost-to-income 59.64%, and operating costs grew 18% YoY. Management said staff reached 12,002 and expected 12,800–12,900 by year-end, below its earlier 13,000 aspiration.
DCB Bank Ltd.whatChanged: Q2 ROA crossed 1% and asset-quality ratios improved, while NIM fell to 3.3% due to excess liquidity carried during the quarter. Management expects Q3/Q4 NIM improvement as excess liquidity reduces and floating-rate loans reprice, but did not issue a revised ROE target pending potential capital actions.
risks: Management cited low-yield excess liquidity from FCNR(B) inflows as the main Q2 NIM drag; projected margin recovery depends on loan repricing and deposit-cost reductions.

Gold loans were 23% of assets, about 70% inorganic via co-lending/DA; management’s stated ceiling is 25%. Slippages in partner-originated gold loans do not always follow the bank’s 1-DPD collection cadence.
SMAs remain the main ECL uncertainty; model work is ongoing. Management cited ₹218 Cr of floating provisions and a secured book, but did not quantify the final ECL requirement.

sectorSummary.overview: Loan growth and profitability improved across the ten reviewed banks, supported by secured lending and better asset quality. Deposit competition, funding mix and ECL preparation remain key constraints. FCNR-linked balances lift some reported growth rates, while margin trajectories differ across lenders.

trends.text: Banks expand secured retail, MSME or gold lending while adjusting portfolio mix.
Banks improve asset-quality ratios or strengthen provision coverage.

tailwinds.text: Loan growth and higher operating income support profit growth.
Recoveries, collection discipline and stronger coverage support credit performance.

headwinds.text: Deposit competition and changes in funding mix create margin-management pressure.
ECL transition requires provisioning or capital planning, with final effects dependent on implementation.

opportunities.text: Branch expansion and a broader retail liability franchise can support more balanced growth.
Asset repricing and deployment of temporary liquidity can help margins recover.

risks.text: FCNR and IBU balances materially affect headline growth or margins; domestic and adjusted bases differ.
Gold-price volatility and rising gold exposure require disciplined collateral monitoring.

insights.text: TMB raises FY27 deposit and advances growth floors to 20%+ and 22%+; KVB lifts its annual NIM outlook above 4%.
DCB misses its Q2 NIM-rise expectation, while IDFC First expects recovery toward 5.8% by Q4.
